During FY2025-26, the Company recognised a provision of ₹2.905 Mn relating to incremental gratuity obligations arising from the revised definition of ‘wages' expected to apply upon implementation of the Code.
Growth & demand: According to the World Travel & Tourism Council, the sector contributed approximately US$ 263.6 billion to the Indian economy in 2025 - a growth of 7.3% against a global average of 4.1% - accounting for close to 6.6% of national GDP and supporting more than 46 million livelihoods.

The Council expects this contribution to rise to about US$ 286.1 billion in 2026 on growth of 8.5%, and to reach nearly US$ 527 billion by 2036, by which time India is projected to move from the tenth- to the fourth-largest travel and tourism economy in the world.

Against this, the Indian economy sustained its position among the fastest-growing large economies, with growth of approximately 7.4% estimated for the year, supported by resilient services and manufacturing activity, consumption-led demand and continued public capital expenditure.
Margins & costs: Your Company has expanded margins substantially on a lower revenue base, which is the direct outcome of a deliberate shift towards higher-yield retail products, disciplined control over operating and establishment costs, closer attention to branch and channel economics, and improved realisation across the foreign exchange and remittance book.
